summary: A note from BBN proposing three aids to improved network operation. The first reserves 7 to 8 a.m. Eastern time every Tuesday for IMP software reloads, since the network never sleeps and downtime is hard to schedule. The other items are further operational improvements.

eli5.summary: The network helpers pick one regular early hour every week to restart machines, so everyone knows when a short break might happen.

questions: what is an imp going down message
subtitle: BBN reserves Tuesday mornings for IMP reloads, adds warnings before shutdowns and reworks the IMP-to-Host messages.

tldr.problem: The ARPA Network never sleeps, so it was hard to find a time to load new IMP software without disrupting someone, and the IMP-to-Host error messages were imprecise or ambiguous.
tldr.mechanism: BBN reserves 7 A.M. to 8 A.M. eastern time every Tuesday for IMP reloads, extends the IMP-Going-Down message to carry a reason and timing, and revises the IMP-to-Host message types on August 14, 1972.
tldr.outcome: A news service was also started. RFC 394 is listed as updating this note.

today: The metadata lists no formal status for RFC 381, and it says the note is updated by RFC 394. It records a 1972 operating practice and message layout for the ARPA Network.

sections.title: Scheduled Software Maintenance
sections.content:
As the network grew, BBN found it difficult to slot in new software without disrupting anyone. There is always traffic between the machines at MIT and almost always between the AMES TIP and IMP, since the sun never sets on the ARPA Network. So BBN reserves 7 A.M. to 8 A.M. eastern time every Tuesday for reloading IMPs. It will probably not use the period every week, but it reserves it. This is on top of the several hours a month already scheduled at each site for hardware preventative maintenance.

Emergency restarts and reloads can still happen, and a restart will be preceded by several minutes of warning with an IMP-Going-Down message. In every case where the IMP is shut down intentionally, a type 2 IMP-to-Host message is sent about 30 seconds before it goes down. An IMP may crash too quickly to warn anyone, but it will never be intentionally shut down that way.
sections.eli5: Every Tuesday morning at seven the helpers might switch off a machine for a little while. They only do it at that time so that nobody is surprised.

sections.title: IMP-to-Host Messages
sections.content:
Users had long complained that IMP-to-Host error messages were not precise enough. The new meanings, which include the additions proposed in RFC 312, take effect on August 14, 1972. Hosts are encouraged to update their NCPs by then; unmodified NCPs will probably keep working, but each site should check.

The generalized type 2 IMP Going Down message uses bits 17 to 32. Bits 17,18 say why (01 scheduled hardware PM, 10 scheduled software reload, 11 emergency reload or restart), bits 19 to 22 say how soon in 5 minute units, and bits 23 to 32 say how long in 5 minute units. All bits zero means going down in 30 seconds. Hosts and the TIP should use it to remind their users.

The changes in summary: there is now exactly one IMP-to-Host message for each regular Host-to-IMP message; types 1, 2, 7 and 9 carry extra information; type 10 is added; types 3 and 6 are discarded. Type 9 now distinguishes, for example, a message too long (more than 8095 bits) from one too slow (more than 15 seconds between first and last bit).
sections.eli5: The machine used to say only that something went wrong. Now it says what went wrong and when it will switch off, like a teacher giving a reason and a time instead of just saying no.

sections.title: Network News Service
sections.content: The third aid is a network news service. TIP users read the news by typing the command @NEWS. Users of other hosts can get it by ICPing to socket 15600031 (octal) at the BBN Tenex. The note ends by asking for further suggestions to improve network operation.
sections.eli5: There is now a bulletin board for the network. You can read it by typing a short command, and others can visit the right door number.
